recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless the work group separately changes ElementDefinition.base semantics or snapshot generation rules for choice elements.
issue_request: FHIR-6066 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core profiles issue asking that a derived profile constraining a type-specific choice element, such as MedicationStatement.effectivePeriod, not imply that other base [x] types are removed from the snapshot. The approved resolution was to add basePath, baseMin, and baseMax to ElementDefinition.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 5924. Git-svn history shows ddb1f8c4e0916fada828b645a84c2c90f59329e2 (#6066, svn r5923) adding ElementDefinition.base and initial population, followed by 74950f48e21290a8d95baa474e74c2d2d3034e11 (#6066, svn r5924) adding ElementDefinition.base invariants.
additional_context: The current model represents the flat resolution names as ElementDefinition.base.path, ElementDefinition.base.min, and ElementDefinition.base.max. FHIR-6093 and FHIR-6340 are the same published change family and are already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-8310 is another same-family issue audited opportunistically here. No direct Zulip or Confluence records were found that alter the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made because current ElementDefinition source defines the 0..1 base component with required path/min/max children, current StructureDefinition snapshots require base metadata, and current choice-element narrative says type-specific elements do not constrain allowed types by themselves and that the original [x] element is always represented in snapshots.
